title: From Task Mixtures to Specialized Experts
abstract: arXiv:2610.00580v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In collaborative foundation model fine-tuning, client data is rarely homogeneous. Instead, clients typically possess unknown mixtures of distinct data distributions, or tasks. Conventional federated learning primarily addresses heterogeneity across clients without explicitly resolving latent task mixtures within each client. We study this setting as compound heterogeneity, where data is heterogeneous both across and within clients. We study adaptation over a common frozen representation and show that, when tasks share the same feature geometry, the optimal model for a client's task mixture under squared loss is a convex combination of the optimal models for its underlying tasks. Thus, a single locally trained model represents the client's overall task mixture, while individual inputs may be drawn from different underlying task distributions. translated_title: 从任务混合到专业化专家
translated_abstract: 在协作式基础模型微调中，客户端数据很少是同质的。相反，客户端通常拥有不同数据分布（即任务）的未知混合。传统联邦学习主要解决客户端之间的异构性问题，而没有显式解析每个客户端内部的潜在任务混合。我们将这种设置称为复合异构性，即数据在客户端之间和客户端内部都是异构的。我们研究了在共同冻结表示上的适配问题，并证明当任务共享相同的特征几何结构时，在平方损失下客户端任务混合的最优模型是其底层任务最优模型的凸组合。因此，单个本地训练的模型即可代表客户端的整体任务混合，而单个输入可能来自不同的底层任务分布。这促使我们将输入路由到专业化专家，并且我们证明，当任务最优解形成……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文研究联邦学习中的复合异构性问题，证明当任务共享相同特征几何结构时，客户端任务混合的最优模型是其底层任务最优模型的凸组合，并据此提出将输入路由到专业化专家的适配方法。
en_tdlr: This paper studies compound heterogeneity in federated learning, showing that when tasks share the same feature geometry, the optimal model for a client's task mixture is a convex combination of the optimal models for its underlying tasks, motivating routing inputs to specialized experts.
